name: Fibre and yarn import
candidate_data: SSB 08801 (HS 50-55 fibre and yarn; woven fabric and retail yarn excluded)
note: HS 56, high-tenacity filament yarn (5402.10/11/19/20), nylon net twine (5402.61), other single synthetic filament yarn (5402.49) and polypropylene staple fibre (5503.40) are outside the scope: they go to ropes, nets, nonwovens and technical products. Retail yarn goes to DI.RT as product YA

name: Fabric import
candidate_data: SSB 08801 (woven fabric in HS 50-55, HS 58 and 60)
note: HS 59 (coated and technical fabrics) is outside the scope

name: Finished textile products import
note: Net weight as declared; includes non-textile parts (buttons/zips/soles). Retail yarn is product YA

name: Private imports
candidate_data: SSB 05678 (cross-border day trips total 2004-2022) and 14221 (clothing and shoes 2023-2025); NOK-to-kg via 08801 unit values x retail markup
note: Not in trade statistics; small (about 0.2-0.5 kt/yr); purchases on overnight travel not covered

name: Direct online imports
candidate_data: Tolletaten VOEC data for HS 61/62/63 2022-2025 via NORSUS 2026; Watson et al. 2020 (3300 t in 2018); SSB 08801 codes 99603000 (VOEC total 2023-)
note: Low-value shipments are not in 08801 under HS codes; see claude_tekst/2026-09-29_lavverdisendinger_VOEC_og_klesimport.md

name: Used textile import
candidate_data: SSB 08801 (HS 6309 and 6310 import)
note: Used clothing (6309, 0.02-0.35 kt) goes to second-hand sales; rags (6310, 1.1-2.1 kt, mostly wiping rags) are discarded with the sorting residues (D32)

name: Norwegian raw wool
candidate_data: Totalkalkylen for jordbrukssektoren (Budsjettnemnda for jordbruket/NIBIO), 1959-2026
note: Greasy wool as weighed in. Animalia/Norilia annual reports for checking

name: Yarn to textile manufacturing
candidate_data: Balance of MA.FI; SSB 10455 (Prodcom, yarn produced in large enterprises 2008-) for checking

name: Domestic hand knitting yarn
candidate_data: SSB Industristatistikk Varetall 1988-1989 (5109.10) and SSB 10455 (Prodcom 13.10.50.50, 2008-2023 with gaps), large units only; SNL (about 1000 t per year); Sandnes Garn (about 600 t)
note: Product YA only. Interpolated over 1990-2007, when SSB published no commodity figures. Uncertainty skewed upwards because small units are missing

name: Fibre and yarn export
candidate_data: SSB 08801 (HS 50-55 fibre and yarn export, incl. greasy wool 5101; high-tenacity filament yarn excluded)
note: Greasy wool is 90-100 % of Norwegian wool since 2007. Yarn export may include re-export of yarn spun abroad

name: Wool scouring loss
candidate_data: Greasy wool scoured in Norway (Totalkalkylen + SSB 08801 greasy wool trade, period means) x loss share (Norwegian Wool Book)
note: Grease, suint and dirt, not textile. Released to wastewater; treatment is not modelled (D35)

name: Domestic finished products
candidate_data: Balance of MA.TX; product shares from SSB Industristatistikk Varetall 1988-1989 and Prodcom 10455 2008-2011 (scripts/derive_domestic_product_mass.py)
note: Mass shares per product interpolated between 1988, 1989 and 2009 (mean of 2008, 2009 and 2011 per commodity) and held after 2009 (D26)

name: Textile export
candidate_data: SSB 08801 (fabric export: woven fabric in HS 50-55, HS 58 and 60)
note: Fabric only. Exports of finished products stay with DI.RT, because the trade statistics do not separate re-export from Norwegian production (D6)

name: Preconsumer production waste
candidate_data: SSB 08604 (2008, 2015) and 14457 (2015, 2022): textile waste generated by NACE 13-15, rounded to whole kt
note: Waste per kt of MA.TX input at the anchor years; before 2008 it follows the input with 2008 as reference

name: Production waste to recycling
candidate_data: de Sadeleer & Rubach 2026, fig. 3-8 and 3-9: NTG intake of production waste (mainly wool production) 20 t (2024) and 39 t (2025); recycled share as for all NTG intake
note: Zero before 2024 (D34)

name: Sales to households
candidate_data: Balance of DI.RT
note: Key inflow to the in-use stock

name: Sales to institutions and businesses
candidate_data: Share of workwear/linen in supply; public procurement data (Doffin/DFØ); industry reports

name: Export of finished textile products
candidate_data: SSB 08801 (HS 61, 62, 63, 64, 57, 9404.30/40/90 and retail yarn export)
note: Includes re-export and returns from online sales, and retail yarn spun in Norway

name: Unsold goods discarded
candidate_data: Share of clothing, household textiles and footwear placed on the market: lognormal, 95 % interval 0.2-9 % (survey minimums of Watson et al. 2020 and Rubach et al. 2023 to EEA 2024), median 1.3 % (geometric mean); SOA 2022 found at least 0.8 % overstock
note: Clothing, household textiles and footwear (D38). Destroyed goods are commercial waste and not in the pick analyses of household waste, so there is no double counting

name: Unsold goods donated
candidate_data: Watson et al. 2020 (one collector received about 600 t from retailers in 2018); Rubach et al. 2023 (collectors received about 200 t in 2022)
note: Clothing only. Per kt of clothing imports in the anchor years, so it follows the clothing imports (D27). Mostly exported with HS 6309, so it is subtracted from collection from households

name: Separate collection from households
candidate_data: SSB 08801 export of HS 6309+6310 + share kept in Norway (Watson 2020, NORSUS 2023, NORSUS 2026), minus unsold goods donated by retailers
note: Anchor years only - interpolation between anchors. Clipped at 0 if donations exceed export plus retained

flow_code: US.HH-WM.RS-Reusable textiles in residual and bulky waste-TOT
name: Reusable textiles in residual and bulky waste
candidate_data: Pick analyses (Mepex/Avfall Norge) x SSB household waste amounts; Reusable share of pick analyses: Laitala et al. 2012 (via Huygens et al. 2023), Rubach et al. 2023, de Sadeleer & Rubach 2026
note: D18. CORE group only: residual textiles x reusable share; CA/TA/OM are counted as worn

flow_code: US.HH-WM.RS-Worn textiles in residual and bulky waste-TOT
name: Worn textiles in residual and bulky waste
candidate_data: Pick analyses (Mepex/Avfall Norge) x SSB household waste amounts; Reusable share of pick analyses: Laitala et al. 2012 (via Huygens et al. 2023), Rubach et al. 2023, de Sadeleer & Rubach 2026
note: D18. CORE residual textiles not reusable, plus CA/TA/OM discarded by the household cohort model (lifetimes)

name: Fibre release in laundry
candidate_data: Laundry mass per inhabitant (Mepex 2014 after Pakula & Stamminger 2010) x SSB population x release from real soiled laundry (Lant et al. 2020, 114 ppm); Mepex 2014 (600 t synthetic) for sensitivity only
note: Natural fibres release about 20 times more per kg than synthetic (Lant et al. 2020, 2022), split in the fibre layer (D37). Released to wastewater; treatment is not modelled (D35)

flow_code: US.HH-EN.AI-Fibre release to air and dust-TOT
name: Fibre release to air and dust
candidate_data: Release during wear at the level of the release in laundry (factor 1, 0.3-3; De Falco et al. 2020), minus the share vacuumed; plus tumble dryer exhaust (Cummins et al. 2023)
note: No Norwegian data. The vacuumed part goes to WM.RS as household dust fibres (D37). Not followed further (D35)

name: Institutional textile waste
candidate_data: Cohort model of sales to institutions and businesses with lifetimes per product (parameters/lifetimes.csv); SSB 10513 cannot separate textiles from mixed business waste
note: No discard statistics for the sector, so an exception to D8 (D29). Sacks discarded in the year supplied (D13)

name: Fibre release in industrial laundry
candidate_data: Same release per kt textile in use as household laundry (D37), applied to the textile stock of the US.IC cohort model
note: No Norwegian data; more frequent washing and filters in industrial laundries pull in opposite directions (D29). Released to wastewater; treatment is not modelled (D35)

name: Institutional textiles to recycling
candidate_data: de Sadeleer & Rubach 2026, fig. 3-8 and 3-9: NTG intake from industry (mainly hotels and health care) 75 t (2024) and 358 t (2025); recycled share as for all NTG intake
note: Household textiles (HT) only; zero before 2024 (D34)

name: Export of unsorted collected textiles
candidate_data: SSB 08801 (HS 6309/6310 export); collector reports; NORSUS 2023 (about 85 % exported)
note: HS 6309 export may also contain sorted grades - split needed

name: Collected textiles to domestic sorting
candidate_data: Balance of CO.CO

name: Sorted for domestic secondhand sales
candidate_data: Collector annual reports

name: Sorted for recycling
candidate_data: Watson et al. 2020 (93 t of 467 t rejects from domestic sorting in 2018); de Sadeleer & Rubach 2026 (142 t from households recycled at NTG in 2025)
note: Share of the rejects from domestic sorting: 20 % (2018), 39 % (2025), held before 2018 (D34)

name: Sorting residues
candidate_data: Reject share from collector reports
note: Rejects from domestic sorting not recycled, and imported rags

name: Secondhand sales to households
candidate_data: Balance of CO.RE
note: Re-enters the in-use stock

name: Domestic incineration
candidate_data: Balance of WM.RS; SSB 10513 treatment by material

name: Residual waste export for incineration
candidate_data: SSB 13035 (KOSTRA): residual waste exported / residual waste total, 2015-2025
note: Mainly to Sweden

name: Landfilling of textiles
candidate_data: SSB 05281 (1995-2011) and 10513 (2012-); earlier years extrapolated
note: Dominant route before 2009 landfill ban - important for the time series

name: Recycled fibre to domestic spinning
candidate_data: de Sadeleer & Rubach 2026: Norsk Tekstilgjenvinning (NTG, Sandefjord) recycled 93 t in 2024 and 364 t in 2025 mechanically to fibre for spinning, sold to Norwegian and European customers
note: Norwegian share of NTG fibre 50 % (0-100 %); zero before 2024 (D34)

name: Export for recycling
candidate_data: Balance of WM.RC: everything recycled before NTG (2024), and the part of NTG fibre not sold in Norway
note: Clipped at 0 (D34)

name: Tumble dryer lint
candidate_data: Laundry mass x households with a tumble dryer (SSB via SNL: 44 % 1996, 47 % 2012) x share of loads dried x release in drying (Cummins et al. 2023, 256-342 ppm) x share caught on the filter (86-91 %)
note: Mostly cotton (Lant et al. 2022). Emptied into residual waste; counted as fines, not textile, in pick analyses, so not double counted (D37)

name: Household dust fibres
candidate_data: Release during wear (see Fibre release to air and dust) x share vacuumed (assumption 0.8, 0.5-0.95)
note: No measurements of textile fibre mass in vacuum cleaner bags found. Goes with residual waste (D37)

name: Returns of direct online purchases
candidate_data: Direct online imports (VOEC) x return share (0.2, 0.05-0.5: EEA about 20 % for clothing bought online, Zalando about 50 %, Temu and Shein probably lower)
note: VOEC figures are deliveries to Norway; returns to foreign web shops leave the country (D38)

flow_code: US.HH-WM.RS-Household textiles in commercial and bulky waste-TOT
name: Household textiles in commercial and bulky waste
candidate_data: Danish analogy: bulky waste taken directly to incineration or private sorting, about 1 kg textiles per inhabitant (Watson et al. 2018, MST); Mepex/Avfall Norge pick analyses of commercial waste (requested)
note: D42. Household textiles collected as commercial waste (moving, estates, skips, bulky waste outside municipal recycling stations), not in the household pick analyses. 0 in the main result (D8), 1 kg per inhabitant in the structural run; in the future module the gap between the scaled cohort model and a realistic stock growth

flow_code: CO.SO-RW.RW-Export of sorted textiles for reuse-TOT
name: Export of sorted textiles for reuse
candidate_data: Future module only: sorted for reuse beyond the Norwegian second-hand market (X13)
note: Phase D step 3. 0 in the history, where exports of HS 6309 count as unsorted (D17); in the future what is sorted in Norway for reuse beyond the domestic second-hand market
